payload.description:
Phase S's exercised-or-unproven gate. Filed 2026-08-03; it was a row in the plan with no bead.

No release tag while a capability the repo advertises has zero executions in the ledger. This is the gate that would have caught permissions-check, the vacuous import contract, vulture and recall_eval - each of which passed every existing gate while doing nothing.

It is the deterministic form of the quality-gate rule that a capability claim on a consumer-facing surface must be exercised before it is published: a claim in code is caught by a gate, one in a README is caught by a consumer. This makes the code half mechanical.

Scope note: the ledger is the existing usage ledger under .basicly/ledger and the run records under .basicly/usage. The gate reads what is already recorded; it does not add telemetry.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/release.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker_usage.py`
- `tests/test_release.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_usage.py`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

**Kept out of scope deliberately** (basicly-23ep): `cli.py` is over four thousand lines and
reading it would dominate the working set. If the refusal needs a CLI wiring point, add it as a
one-line call into `release.py` and declare the addition on the bead rather than widening scope
mid-flight - widening is what basicly-tcmy.5 did, and it moved a global constant and failed a
gate for two sibling lanes.

**Scope addition declared** (basicly-irrm, 2026-08-04): `tests/test_tracker_usage.py` and
`CHANGELOG.md` were added to the list above. `tracker_usage.py` gains a public
`surface_executions`, and this repo keeps a module's unit tests in that module's own test
file, so its tests belong there rather than in `test_release.py`. The `CHANGELOG` entry is
the `[Unreleased]` line for a user-visible refusal, which `basicly release` reads from the
tagged commit and so can only be curated before the tag. `cli.py` stays out: the refusal
wires through `blocking_reasons`, which the CLI already calls, so no CLI edit was needed.
payload.title: Refuse a release tag while a shipped capability has zero recorded executions

## Trigger

When a tracker-only source-checkout push reruns the unchanged code suite, I want equivalent native-push inputs to reuse trusted results, so I can avoid the demonstrated 109-second repeat.

## Steps to Reproduce

The v0.26.6 source/tag push established passing evidence, then the final tracker-only main push reran pytest while all three compiler checks reused. See the final-push evidence and correction on basicly-h79lott.5. Compare direct and actual native hook inputs by component hash, establish the cause, and verify a real metadata-only native push.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner requirement described 2026-07-31: a tier should be able to fall back, so that if the tier's
model is unavailable on a family the agent still runs on another model of the SAME capability class
rather than failing or silently inheriting. Split out of basicly-kjc5.61 by owner decision to keep that
lane single-model and land on schedule.

All facts below were verified against live vendor docs today, not recalled.

## What each surface can actually express

- **GitHub Copilot / VS Code: an ordered list, natively.** `model` accepts "a single model name
  (string) or a prioritized list of models (array)", documented example
  `model: ['Claude Opus 4.5', 'GPT-5.2']`, tried in order. So copilot can honour a preference chain
  with no work on our side beyond emitting the array.
- **Claude Code: a single value only.** Subagent frontmatter `model` takes `sonnet`/`opus`/`haiku`/
  `fable`, a full model id (`claude-opus-5`), or `inherit`; it defaults to `inherit`. There is no array
  form. Claude Code resolves a subagent's model in this order: (1) the `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`
  env var, (2) the per-invocation `model` parameter, (3) the definition's `model` frontmatter, (4) the
  main conversation's model. Neither (1) nor (2) is usable for per-agent tiers - the env var is
  session-wide across ALL subagents, and the per-invocation parameter is chosen by the orchestrating
  model, not by the harness. So (3) is our only per-agent slot and it holds one value.
- **Claude Code's own degradation is NOT tier-preserving**: a value excluded by the org
  `availableModels` allowlist is skipped and the subagent "runs on the inherited model instead" -
  which may be any tier, higher or lower.

## The trap this bead exists to prevent

The roster's tier table (docs/design/agent-roster-design.md R5) maps the GPT classes as luna=low,
terra=medium, sol=high AND maximum. So an intuitive-sounding chain like "Claude Opus 5, else
GPT-5.6 Terra" **silently demotes a high-tier judgment to medium**. Any fallback list must be
constrained to same-tier members, and the generator should refuse a chain that mixes tiers rather
than trusting the author to get it right.

## The decision to make

1. Does a tier carry an ordered list, or exactly one model? If a list, is it authored per tier in the
   anchor source, or derived from the map by capability class?
2. What does an unavailable tier model mean where the surface cannot express a chain (claude)? The
   repo's standing rule is fail closed on an indeterminate answer, and "cannot tell" must never read
   as "safe to proceed" - so silently inheriting an unknown tier is arguably the wrong default and a
   refusal or a recorded not-honoured marker may be right. basicly-kjc5.59 already establishes the
   record-the-fallback-rather-than-imply-it stance for a family with no slot; reuse it, do not invent
   a second convention.
3. Whether the fallback is worth having at all given it is honourable on exactly one of our two
   required families today.

Both families also expose a REASONING EFFORT axis independent of model choice - Claude Code subagent

## Trigger
The owner, 2026-09-12: build a test that measures how much of the always-on instructions the model actually retains, comparing what the model generates against what the file says, and treat that as more important than a vendor doc.

## Why the old harness could not answer it
`.scripts/recall_eval.py` scored against a hand-maintained anchor list in `recall_rules.toml`. That list rotted: 9 rules had no anchors and 11 had stale text guards, and `--inventory` exited 1 on a clean tree. A hand-maintained inventory is the defect, not the symptom.

## What replaces it
`src/basicly/retention.py` derives the rules from the file itself, so there is no inventory to drift. Scoring is IDF-weighted content-word recall against every line and adjacent line pair of the response, taking the better of the whole rule and its imperative clause. Deterministic, stdlib only, no network.

`.scripts/retention_eval.py` dispatches a cell with the file and a no-guidance control, then reports the rate, the retention curve by position in the file, the per-section table, and each unretained rule beside the closest line in the response.

## Measured 2026-09-12, claude, n=1 per point
| lines | rules | retained | 1st half | 2nd half |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 152 | 59 | 94.9% | 93% | 97% |
| 266 | 74 | 91.9% | 92% | 91% |
| 700 | 130 | 82.3% | 89% | 75% |
| 1667 | 158 | 78.5% | 90% | 67% |

Control arm with no file: 5.1%, so the lift attributable to the file is +89.8 points.

The first half of a file holds near 90% at every length. Only the tail is lost, and the knee is between 266 and 700 lines.

## What bounds the claim
The probe cannot separate "forgot the rule" from "stopped enumerating": response length grew 111, 159, 178, 259 lines while rule count grew 59, 74, 130, 158. n is 1 per point. The scorer is lexical, with a calibrated false-negative near 1 in 6 on a distant paraphrase. The positional finding is a within-response comparison and survives all three caveats; the absolute rates are floors.

## Scope
- `src/basicly/retention.py`
- `.scripts/retention_eval.py`
- `tests/test_retention.py`

payload.description:
Recurring DX friction (hit at least three times: v0.2.0 release tables, basicly-h0f0, and noted again in basicly-yw28 prep). markdownlint MD060 uses the "aligned" table style, so editing any cell in a wide docs table (e.g. the command table in docs/architecture.md, ~490 chars wide) requires re-padding every pipe to match the header column widths, and `markdownlint-cli2 --fix` does NOT auto-repad the aligned style. Widening the FIRST column cascades a re-pad to every row. The reliable fix each time is a hand-run Python script that reads the header pipe columns and rebuilds the edited row.

Pick a durable fix so this stops recurring. Candidate directions: (a) add a small committed `.scripts/` helper that re-pads a markdown table to MD060-aligned style (invoked manually or as a pre-commit auto-fix); (b) relax MD060 for docs (switch the config to a non-aligned table style, or disable MD060) accepting ragged pipes; (c) split the offending wide tables so cells stay short. Evaluate the trade-off (aligned tables read better in raw markdown but cost edit friction).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Editing a wide docs table no longer requires a hand-authored re-pad script: either a committed helper does it, or the lint rule no longer demands aligned pipes.
- The chosen approach is applied to docs/architecture.md's wide tables and markdownlint passes.
- Decision (helper vs relax-rule vs split-tables) recorded.

payload.description:
## Context

Measured by `basicly usage report` on 2026-08-20. The never used list includes **`root-cause`,
`falsify-first`, `repair-in-place`, `validate-as-consumer`, `worktree-isolation` and `decompose-plan`** -
six skills whose triggers describe, almost exactly, the work a full session had just done: a repair
briefed into a lane's own worktree, a consumer validation, five sibling worktrees, a root cause chased
to a control, and a design cut into dispatchable children.

All six were hand rolled instead. The session's briefs re-derived, in prose, guidance the catalog
already ships - and re-derived it **less completely**, because a hand written brief carries what the
author recalled rather than what the skill records.

So the defect is not that the skills are wrong. It is that **nothing makes a skill reachable at the
moment its trigger fires**, and a skill nothing reaches is indistinguishable from a skill that does not
exist. 11 skills have ever been invoked against 32 never invoked; the never used side is where every
process skill sits, while the used side is the four or five a session touches by habit.

Two candidate controls, and this record does not choose. **(a)** The dispatch brief names the skill
whose trigger the unit matches, so an agent is pointed at it by the engine rather than by an author's
memory. **(b)** A retro check that reports, per closed record, whether any skill covering its work type
was invoked - making the gap visible per unit instead of as one aggregate list. Neither is a culling
argument: the earlier reading of that list as culling candidates is what left these six unexercised.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `uv run basicly usage report`.
2. Read the Skills table and the never used list beneath it.
3. Observe root-cause, falsify-first, repair-in-place, validate-as-consumer, worktree-isolation and decompose-plan are all in the never used list.
4. Read those six skills' trigger sections and compare against the work of any recent multi lane session.
5. Observe the triggers match work that was done without them, so the skills were reachable in principle and unreached in fact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a dispatched unit whose work matches a skill trigger when its brief is composed then the brief names that skill - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_dispatch_brief.py -k names_a_skill -q`
- Given a skill has never been invoked when the usage report runs then it is reported as unexercised rather than as a culling candidate, since the two are different claims

## Scope

- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_dispatch_brief.py -k names_a_skill -q`

payload.description: Reported by burndown-chart from a real v0.12.1 to v0.12.2 upgrade and reproduced here as a consumer. .github/workflows/basicly-gates.yml is scaffolded only when absent, and it embeds five uvx --from git+...@vX.Y.Z pins built from the installing engine's own version (scaffolds.DIST_SOURCE). An upgrade converges and leaves all five at the old tag. The next push then runs the OLD engine against a catalog the NEW one installed, and the version-skew guard refuses: four of the five workflow steps fail. Positive control here - a scratch repo installed at 0.12.2, then uvx --from git+...@v0.12.1 basicly check exits 1 with Version skew: the core catalog was installed by basicly 0.12.2 and this is basicly 0.12.1. The guard is right; the interaction is the defect. install is the only thing that knows the new version, the workflow is the only place the pin lives, and install deliberately will not touch it after the first write. Nothing in the install output mentions it and the failure surfaces in CI as version skew rather than as anything a reader connects to the upgrade. .vscode/tasks.json carries the same five pins and the same latent shape - it does not break CI, it silently runs the old engine from a task. release.py already has the narrow machinery for this: PIN_FILES plus PIN_RE_TEMPLATE rewrite only the version substring.
